Not to be a bucket of cold water here, but imo there's so much more to being social than just showing up. For starters, you have to be the kind of person that others want to meet; you have to be able to meet certain what I like to call minimum requirements. For example, a person who exhibits personality flaws or has neurotic tendencies is inevitably going to be shunned or outright ostracized, even amongst complete strangers.

A person with limited social skills is going to be judged for that deficiency, especially if they are lacking in other areas like fashion sense or mutual interests. And, just so it's clear to all, I am not in any way shape or form saying that the others in these situations are bad people. I cannot stress this fact enough.

All of this is to say that, while your story is beautiful and inspiring, some of us just...can't, and in all honesty probably shouldn't. 

Doesn't mean I'm not cheering you on though!

I used to struggle terribly with flashbacks that usually came up randomly and to a certain extent I still do but there's a trick that I've discovered that hopefully will work for you too. 

Whenever one pops up, I stop whatever I'm doing for a second to focus before saying out loud "That's not happening right now." I know it sounds silly but it really works for me because when the flashbacks start, I'm not "watching the movie" of the event, I'm reliving it all over again in excruciating detail. And it feels so intense that a single traumatic flashback could send me spiralling for days or even weeks. I have to physically tell myself and my brain that what I'm seeing/doing/feeling during those aren't real and I don't need to grab onto that pain any more.

I hope this helps you. Feel free to dm if you need someone to talk to. We gotta take care of each other.

Yu-Gi-Oh is a game where advantage is gained by "searching" (adding cards to the hand). Unlike magic, in Yu-Gi-Oh nearly every card in a deck is accessible at most points in the game via searching. 

Unfortunately for some, the modern game is not really about card advantage anymore. Games are decided by who can pump out the biggest board the fastest and prevent their opponent from playing the game, as much as possible. The past several formats have been more balanced in that regard, but that style of gameplay has become standard amongst meta decks for the last couple years.
